item.summary: Cannot enable helium package due to EACCES: permission denied, mkdir '/.cache'

status.description: This issue was once resolved, but the resolution was deemed incorrect. From here issues are either marked assigned or resolved.

comments.comment:
If you experience this problem on docker container image, a workaround is set HOME environtment variable to /zeppelin.

For example

 docker run -p8080:8080 --rm -e HOME=/zeppelin -e ZEPPELIN_HELIUM_REGISTRY=helium,https://s3.amazonaws.com/helium-package/helium.json apache/zeppelin:0.9.0

I checked the env of my container and saw that the HOME is set to /zeppelin (I didn't set it explicitly).
Should I try to set it explicitly?

Thanks for confirming. 

It seems better to set an environment variable in Dockerfile. So it can work without set HOME explicitly.

When I moved from version 0.9.0-preview2 to 0.9.0 I got the same issue again and this time the workaround did not work

This is the new exception:

Caused by: com.github.eirslett.maven.plugins.frontend.lib.TaskRunnerException: 'yarn config set cache-folder /opt/zeppelin/local-repo/helium-bundle/yarn-cache --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/' failed. (error code 1)

I've also run into this problem with the kubernetes zeppelin deploy.

For the 0.9.0 image the home has to be set to '/opt/zeppelin/' as that's the only directory the default 'zeppelin' user has write access on.
I moved to the newer version 0.10.0 and setting the home dir to /opt/zeppelin/ helped fixing the issue
